chapter: Marriages, Tong Funeral and Liberation Music
title: Pianos tuned a half step low
summary: Her father tuned the studio pianos a half step low to save money, which she still adjusts for.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: (fades in) And we are rolling. We are back. So you were talking about your father and pianos?

Well my father was a piano teacher and he taught in the house as well as he would go to people’s houses, you know if they couldn’t come to our house. And he would sit at one piano and the student would sit at the other piano. But the bad thing about this was he had the pianos tuned a half a step low. So that A was Ab, and can you imagine, like, playing a chord on the piano and it’s... you play a triad, say C, E, G, and what you hear is B, D#, F#. That’s how I was raised. I was raised with pianos that were tuned a half step low.
What was his rationale for having them, doing a half step low?
To save money. It doesn’t have to be tuned as often.
Oh. Interesting.
How unmusical could you get.
So this must have played havoc with the years to come just to kind of recondition yourself.
Still does. I have to adjust my brain all the time to my father’s piano.
Wow. I know that, was it, umm, who was it that had an adjustable piano, um...
Someone had an adjustable piano?
Yeah. But it wasn’t necessarily... Yeah, it was... oh god I’m sorry I was
thinking about it and it’s coming to me...
Was it a piece of furniture or was it an electronic thing?
No no no, it was a traditional upright piano there that was set up to be able to shift keys there in a way.
WOW.
Yeah.
Never heard of that.
I’m kind of drawing a blank here. So...
That’s all I wanted to say, I just wanted to mention that.
So we are, we’re in the sixties, correct?
Yes.
